## Result

**This independent attack produced a concrete autonomous memory with noisy controllers and a general theorem that accounts for finite recovery time and rare fault histories. It did not establish a scalable memory against arbitrary quantum noise.**

The strongest fully analyzed physical model uses **six actual qubits**, static interactions involving at most two qubits, and one-qubit dissipation. Under its stated noise model, it preserves an unknown qubit—including entanglement with an external reference—with decoded error below **0.005874** after a storage time \(100/g\). Every controller qubit has continuing \(X\), \(Y\), and \(Z\) faults, each at the same rate as the data’s bit-flip faults.

The basic six-qubit architecture turned out to be prior art. The useful work here is the complete noisy-controller analysis, the finite-response theorem, the full physical-channel calculation, and the stronger construction attempts that expose what still prevents protection against both bit and phase errors. I am **not calling this a foundational breakthrough**.

### Completed files

The report contains the synthesis and full proof appendices. The package includes the report, source, executable calculations, numerical results, comparisons, and failed constructions.

- [Autonomous_Quantum_Memory_20261101.pdf](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_366bdf3d26f08191bbcf4b1c73322e12&account_id=personal)
- [Autonomous_Quantum_Memory_20261101_Proofs_and_Code.zip](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_c54151420768819181d8ea40ae9539d7&account_id=personal)

Both compared devices then have controller onsite energy 32g, while the filter adds three noisy qubits and exchange interactions of strength 16g. The producer therefore does not claim a demonstrated resource advantage.
